newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel rejects U.S. dictates ahead of peace drive.
newsitem.headline: Israel rejects U.S. dictates ahead of peace drive.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took a tough line on Wednesday ahead of a visit by a U.S. mediator, saying Washington could not dictate formulas for reviving Middle East peacemaking.

The remark raised speculation Israel was headed for a clash with its closest ally if Washington urged it to halt Jewish settlement expansion in order to bring Palestinians back to the bargaining table -- a concession Netanyahu has ruled out.

"There are no American client states here," Netanyahu told the newspaper Haaretz in an interview published after the White House announced it was sending envoy Dennis Ross to the region for high-level talks to advance peacemaking.
"The United States is a partner in efforts ...to reach an agreed settlement and the key word is 'agreed'. This must be accomplished through consultation and agreement and not by dictates," he said.
Ross was expected to meet Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat separately on Thursday in talks Israeli officials said would build on peace contacts in Washington this month.

Diplomatic sources have said the United States is drafting an initiative to revive peacemaking stalled since March. This would include an Israeli "pause" in settlement building in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
"There appears to be a clash on the horizon between Israel and the U.S. over settlements unless Netanyahu finds a way to circumvent it," said political analyst Chemi Shalev of the Maariv newspaper.
Shalev said Washington would refrain from imposing a formula on Israel but could present a settlement freeze as "the sine qua non of the whole deal".
"If that happens, Israel would be put on the spot and told if it doesn't agree, the initiative will fail," he told Reuters.
Palestinians say Israeli settlement in the West Bank and Gaza Strip captured in the 1967 Middle East war is aimed at sinking their chances for a Palestinian state.
Under Israel-PLO peace deals, the final status of the West Bank and Gaza Strip is to be negotiated by 1999.
The sides have had some contacts but no formal negotiations since March when bulldozers began carving up a hill in Arab East Jerusalem where Israel plans 6,500 apartments for Jews.
Palestinians have conditioned a renewal of peace talks on an Israeli settlement freeze.

"These are the most important issues in the permanent status negotiations. We cannot negotiate while the settlements are expanding and Arab Jerusalem is shrinking," Palestinian cabinet minister Nabil Shaath told Reuters.
Shaath is one of three Palestinian cabinet ministers implicated on Tuesday in a corruption report that could distract Arafat during Ross's visit.
The Palestinian Legislative Council on Wednesday discussed the report, which called on Arafat to sack his entire cabinet and put at least two ministers suspected of wrongdoing on trial.
Arafat vowed on Tuesday to take "all the necessary measures" to curb corruption but did not say if he would fire cabinet members. The legislature was due to vote on the report.
